* Biogas Boiler
A biogas boiler uses biogas as a gaseous renewable fuel to generate steam or hot water for industrial process heating. Biogas is typically produced through anaerobic digestion of organic materials such as cattle manure, agricultural residues, food waste, sewage or other biodegradable feedstocks. The biogas is cleaned and supplied to a suitable burner or boiler system where combustion produces heat for water or steam generation.

Field
	Value
	Process
	Steam or hot-water generation for industrial process heating applications such as food processing, dairy, textile processing, drying, sterilizing, cooking and chemical processing.
	Temperature
	Suitable for industrial hot-water and steam applications; achievable temperature depends on boiler design, steam pressure and burner configuration.
	Energy source
	Biogas produced through anaerobic digestion. Biogas composition varies with feedstock and normally contains methane and carbon dioxide with smaller quantities of other gases.
	Efficiency
	Typically dependent on boiler design, burner quality, gas composition and operating conditions. A project-specific efficiency should be used where manufacturer or measured data are available.
	CAPEX
	Depends strongly on boiler capacity, biogas cleaning system, gas storage, compression, burner, piping, safety systems and installation requirements. Project-specific vendor quotations should be used for final financial modelling.
	OPEX
	Includes biogas production or procurement, gas cleaning, compression, pumps, water treatment, maintenance, labour and periodic equipment servicing.
	Lifetime
	Typically dependent on boiler construction, operating conditions and maintenance. Project-specific manufacturer data should be preferred.
	Space
	Requires boiler equipment and may require biogas storage, gas cleaning, piping, safety equipment and feedstock or digester infrastructure when biogas is produced on-site.
	Constraints
	Biogas availability, methane concentration, gas pressure, gas cleaning requirements, hydrogen sulfide and moisture removal, storage capacity, feedstock availability, safety requirements, burner compatibility and continuous gas supply.
	Existing equipment replaced
	Can potentially replace coal, diesel, LPG, natural-gas or other fossil-fuel-fired boilers where the required heat output, steam pressure, temperature and reliable biogas supply can be achieved.
	Emissions
	Biogas combustion produces direct CO2 and other combustion emissions. The CO2 from biogenic carbon is treated according to the selected greenhouse-gas accounting methodology. Methane leakage and combustion-related pollutants may require separate accounting.
	Main by-product
	Combustion products. When biogas is produced through anaerobic digestion, the digestion process also produces digestate, which may have potential agricultural or waste-management uses subject to applicable requirements.
	Fuel consumption
	Depends on useful heat demand, biogas lower heating value and boiler efficiency. The basic engineering relationship is V_biogas = Q_useful / (LHV x efficiency), with appropriate unit conversion.
	Main advantage
	Can utilize locally produced renewable biogas and reduce dependence on fossil fuels while providing continuous process heat when a reliable biogas supply is available.
	Main disadvantage
	Requires reliable biogas production or supply, gas cleaning, appropriate storage and safety systems. Biogas composition can vary and methane leakage must be controlled.
	Key calculation
	V_biogas = Q_useful / (LHV x efficiency)
	Where V_biogas = biogas consumption, Q_useful = required useful heat, LHV = lower heating value of biogas, and efficiency = boiler efficiency.

Emission factor reference
	The project knowledge base uses the configured biogas emission factor from emission_factors.json. The current factor is 54.6 tCO2/TJ and the configured NCV is 19.88 MJ/m3. These values must be treated according to the project's selected accounting methodology and source documentation.
